frozenNotice: This addendum stands NEXT to the binding base record and takes nothing away from it. The base record is not edited, not re-sealed and not superseded. House pattern: protocol/early-detection/2.0.0/r2-a1-t173-form-type-counter-addendum.json (sha256 a7002de9b01c83bb025471ce1fc2c32faf3d947ca0f76e99eb4e6b5eb931dcc7), a separate file amending a frozen record without touching it.

authority.scope: Register the EXECUTABLE enforcement anchor of the single-appender rule alongside the documentary anchor already named in the base record.

amends.whatIsAmended: The base record's enforcement.gitPrefixAnchor names exactly one anchor and calls it the enforcement of the rule. That anchor is documentary with respect to the rule's own failure mode. This addendum adds the executable anchor; it removes, replaces and relaxes nothing.
amends.whyTheBaseRecordIsNotEdited: tests/studie-register-single-appender-rule.test.js:212 pins the base record's complete enforcement block via assert.deepEqual. Editing the base record would either turn that pin red or force it to be loosened - both would weaken the rule this addendum strengthens. A separate file is the house-correct route.

documentedBlindness.documentaryAnchor: tests/studie-r1-register.test.js, test 'R1: jede committete Revision ist byte-identisches Praefix der aktuellen'
documentedBlindness.whatItCannotSee: A branch-side ledger append - which is precisely the act the rule forbids. Appending is the one operation the prefix invariant permits: a branch that adds one well-formed entry keeps every committed revision a byte-identical prefix of its own tip, and the chain check lib/studie-verfassung.js::pruefeZugriffsRegister passes too, because the entry is genuinely well formed. Prefix and chain catch rewrites, deletions and insertions. Nothing caught the append.
documentedBlindness.provenNotAsserted: The blindness is not claimed in prose. It is EXECUTED on a hermetic sabotage fixture (a throwaway git repository built inside the test) and observed, in tests/studie-register-single-appender-rule.test.js, test 'T172 probe: chain check and git-prefix anchor are BLIND to that same append'.

module.sha256Basis: SHA-256 over the file bytes with CRLF normalised to LF; this path is not pinned to LF by .gitattributes, so a Windows checkout must not decide the verdict.
module.decisionRule: Look at what the head added since it forked off base (three-dot range). If the ledger is not among those paths there is nothing to judge. If it is, the range must contain the ledger and NOTHING else - the ledger-only mini-PR the base record's branchWorkSequence prescribes.
module.rangeWideNotPerCommit: Deliberate. Splitting the append into its own commit inside a study branch is the obvious evasion; a per-commit check would wave it through. The probe executes that evasion and shows it caught.
module.failsClosed: A guard that cannot run says so. resolveBaseRef rethrows anything that is not a plain 'ref does not exist' miss, and checkSingleAppender refuses a backslash-joined ledgerRel instead of returning a clean verdict for the wrong reason.

probe.sha256Basis: SHA-256 over the file bytes with CRLF normalised to LF.
probe.kind: executed sabotage probe on a hermetic temporary git repository; the real ledger on main is never touched and nothing is pushed from the sabotage branch
executedProbes: T172 probe: an executed branch-side ledger append is CAUGHT
T172 probe: splitting the append into its own commit does not buy an escape
T172 probe: chain check and git-prefix anchor are BLIND to that same append
T172 probe: the clean branch and the prescribed mini-PR stay GREEN
T172 probe: the guard refuses to run blind
T172: the live checkout carries no branch-side ledger append
probe.bothDirections: The probe pins red AND green: the violation is caught, and the two legitimate shapes (a branch that never touches the ledger, and the prescribed ledger-only mini-PR) stay green. A guard that only ever fires proves nothing about the route it is supposed to permit.

executableEnforcementAnchor.honestLimit: The guard reads git topology, not intent. A ledger-only branch that is never merged before the access happens looks exactly like a legitimate mini-PR here. That hole is closed by the independent server-time proof scripts/studie-r1-serverzeit.js, which requires the entry to be observable on main before the first access. The limit is stated in the module header and is not repaired by this addendum.

guardedBy.purpose: Holds the registration to the files: the hashes above are re-computed from the working tree, the base record's byte state is pinned, and every probe name listed here must exist verbatim in the probe file. A registration nobody re-measures is the same documentary anchor this addendum exists to supplement.

notAWeakening: No rule, threshold, gate or decision rule of the base record is touched.
No check is removed, skipped or made more tolerant; the documentary anchor keeps its full standing.
The access ledger is not appended to, not edited and not re-hashed by this addendum.
No seal, no hash manifest and no confirmatory verdict is changed.
The endtest window is not named, not counted and not opened.
explicitNonClaims: The addendum does not claim the rule is now unevadable. It claims one named blindness is closed by an executed check, and states the remaining topological limit.
It does not close the residual debt of the e4d deviation record and does not re-open it.
It authorises no data access and no ledger entry.
It makes no statement about any study result, signal or outcome.
